input.question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?
input.ground_truth: It doesn't really matter what they're saying. The point is to get you psyched up and excited so you're more prone to buying something. All about energy levels moreso than actual content. If you go to some auctions for more expensive items (luxury cars, art, etc.), then you'll probably hear a slower auctioneer and a more thorough description of the item.

Question: besides the dollar amount, what the hell are autioneers actually saying?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you and your friend are playing a game where you both want the same cool toy. An "auctioneer" is like the person who helps you both talk about who wants the toy more and how much they want to pay for it.

When the auctioneer talks really fast and says a bunch of numbers and words, they are not just saying how much money you should give. They are also telling you:

- Who is still playing (who is still bidding)
- How much money each person is offering (but they say it quickly!)
- When you need to say how much you want to pay (they say "I have $10!" or "Do I hear $15?")
- If someone gives up (they say "Sold!" when no one else wants to pay more)
- Sometimes they make it sound exciting or fun to keep everyone interested

So, besides the numbers (dollar amount), the auctioneer is also telling everyone what is happening in the game, who is still in, and what to do next!
